entry.summary: Australians may need an online e-visa; a tourist visa on entry needs a non-Egyptian credit card or US dollars cash.
entry.other: Crossing at Taba from Israel without a visa gives a Sinai-only stamp. Land border travel needs permission from the Ministry of Interior's Travel Permits Department.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Egyptian Pound (EGP). You can take up to EGP 5000 in cash when travelling to or from Egypt. You must declare all foreign currency amounts over USD 10,000 or equivalent. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you're visiting as a tourist, you may need to pay USD or euros for your accommodation. Most well-established hotels and resorts accept card payments. ATMs are available in most established areas. Consult your financial institution prior to your travel. - Embassy or Consulate of Egypt - Scams that affect travellers

laws.rule: Authorities may treat public comments that criticise the Egyptian Government, security forces or Islam as illegal. Police have arrested foreigners who published critical social media posts, including 'liking' pages.
laws.heading: Criticising authority

laws.rule: Possessing illegal drugs can lead to the death penalty, long prison sentences or deportation.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Egyptian family law differs significantly from Australian law, particularly in relation to divorce, child custody and support. Before you become involved in a local legal matter, get legal advice, including for family and business legal matters. It's important to know your rights and responsibilities under Egyptian law.
laws.heading: Family law

laws.rule: If you want to get married in Egypt, check the legal requirements before you travel. You can do this either through the Australian Embassy in Cairo or the Egyptian Embassy in Canberra.
laws.heading: Marriage laws

laws.rule: It's illegal to: have sexual relations outside marriage take photos of bridges and canals, including the Suez Canal take photos of military personnel, buildings or equipment The Egyptian Government doesn't interfere with the practice of Christianity, but preaching is illegal. If you're considering preaching, seek local legal advice beforehand. Follow the advice of local authorities.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: There's little public acceptance of homosexuality. LGBTQIA+ individuals face significant social stigma and discrimination. Same-sex relationships aren't explicitly illegal, however, people have been charged with 'committing an indecent act in public and breaching public morality' and penalised with imprisonment. LGBTQIA+ people and advocacy groups have reported harassment, intimidation, arrests, and other forms of abuse, including by police. There are also reports that authorities have used social media, dating websites, and mobile phone apps to entrap people suspected of being homosexual or transgender in the act of 'debauchery', which is a crime that has severe penalties.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ laws

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws during this time. Avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public or in front of people who are fasting.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: You can't drive in Egypt on your Australian driver's licence. Before arriving, get an international driver's permit and get an embassy or consulate of Egypt to certify it.
laws.heading: Driving permit

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Orthodox Easter is observed by the Christian community, as is Christmas Day, which is celebrated on 7 January in Egypt. The work week is Sunday to Thursday. Egypt's customs, laws, and regulations follow Islamic practices and beliefs. Exercise common sense and discretion in dress and behaviour. Dress conservatively. Knee-length or longer dresses and long sleeves are preferable for women, and men should not wear shorts outside tourist areas. Respect religious and social traditions to avoid offending local sensitivities. Overt public displays of intimate affection are frowned upon in Egyptian culture. If in doubt, seek local advice.
culture-and-protocol.note: Read from the Australian Government's description of local customs.
